data.name: Sadaqat
data.gender_notes: Sadaqat is used as a أنثى name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sadaqat is an Arabic name that means 'charity', 'benevolence'. It is derived from the word sidq which means 'truthfulness', 'sincerity'. The name Sadaqat carries the meaning “Charity, Benevolence” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Sadaqat usually hope their child will grow to embody charity, benevolence and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Being truthful and sincere in your actions and deeds.
data.etymology: Sadaqat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Charity, Benevolence.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sadaqat total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_english.name: Sadaqat
in_english.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'S-D-Q', Sadaqat signifies the act of giving charity, truthfulness, and sincerity. In Islamic tradition, it relates to spending in the way of Allah and doing good deeds. The name holds spiritual significance, reflecting the values of generosity and moral integrity.

data.cultural_impact: Sadaqat holds significant cultural importance in Islamic communities, particularly during the holy month of Ramadan. It is one of the five pillars of Islam, and practicing sadaqah (giving to charity) is considered a fundamental act of social responsibility and a reminder of the blessings we have been given. Charitable gifts, especially those made in secret, are regarded as a highly virtuous act, promoting goodwill, kindness, and unity within the community.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Sadaqat represents selflessness, generosity, and submission to God. It is a way to connect with the divine, purify the soul, and cultivate spiritual growth. Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Save yourself from the Hellfire even by giving a morsel of food in charity." (Bukhari) Giving to those in need not only makes a practical difference in their lives but also serves to elevate the giver's spiritual plane.
